title: Choose the contractor by the kind of work
description:
Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** Harbour picks a model for each step. The building step defaults to Haiku, and in John's words that's "precisely because we give it a strict list". On 6 November an essay went the same way and came out stiff and list-shaped. On 7 November it went to one writer on Opus, with one fresh reader. That took about eleven minutes and read far better. The brief was plainer too, but the contractor mattered.

**What we want.** The kind of work chooses the contractor. For writing for people (essays, papers, guides, the words on a page), John wants "opus at a minimum", with a fresh reader afterwards who doesn't have our context. The essay that worked went straight to one writer and one reader, not through the stages built for code. Whether every writing ticket should skip those stages is yours to judge. Judging work, such as the readers who score a change from its code and the look-first step, is judgement too, so give it a model to match. Code goes through the pipeline as it does now.

Keep in mind that as briefs get plainer (the rest of this round is about that), "a strict list" describes less of the building work. Say in the pull request whether the code default still fits. Don't change it unasked.

A ticket shows which path and which model it will get before it runs, and a person can change either.

**Appetite:** err larger.

**Done looks like:** an essay ticket filed in plain words is written on Opus or better and read fresh, without anyone setting the model by hand. A code ticket runs as it does today.

parent.title: Harbour carries the loop (round 1): the hand carries less

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4348 @ e63c2f69d

**Routing has no idea what a ticket is about.** Every model choice resolves from the job *kind* (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:569`: explicit > preset > anchor > job row > group row). An essay and a code change both reach the builder as `implementation`, so they get the same row. Putting an essay on Opus is a hand setting, as it was on 7 Nov. "Kind of work" is a new axis that belongs to the ticket, and nothing stores it.

**The path is harder to show than the model.** `GET /api/dispatch/preview` (`routes/dispatch.js:607`) already shows the model for one known kind. But nobody knows the path in advance. The stage selector (`lib/stage-router.js`) picks one step at a time, using rules built for code: rule 8 sends anything without a plan to `plan`, then plan-review, then implementation. A writer → reader path means either adding kinds or putting a branch ahead of the selector. New kinds touch `DISPATCH_KINDS`, the census, the prompt size budget and the byte-pinned selector prompt. A branch touches less, but it's a second router.

**Who decides it's writing?** A ticket "filed in plain words" has no label. So the call falls to a model (triage or the selector) or to a rule about what the ticket touches. Essays aren't pure prose: v3 and v4 both changed `charts.mjs` and SVGs, and a path that skips review skips that code as well. Wrong guesses must be cheap to spot and fix.

**A "fresh reader" goes against how runs are built.** Every dispatch adds proxy context and points the agent at the brief. A deliberately fresh reader has to opt out of both (`appendProxyContext: false`, no brief, no trail). `review` and `retrospective-audit` don't fit: both are long templates about PRs and ledgers.

**Judging.** The `judge` group (review, plan-review, retro, audit) can be given a model with a data change. But survey-task and survey-place, the nearest thing to "look first", sit in `plan`. The blind readers are scripts with no job of their own. Moving a job to another group is a data change. Giving the readers a job takes code. Groups are coarse: `make` also holds `close-out`.

**Traps.** "Opus or better" includes Fable, and the runner kit can't map `fable` (`runner-kit/runner.mjs:697`). The Haiku default for code lives in workspace routing data, not in the repo, so whether it "still fits" is a judgement call. No diff will show it.

**What I'd do first.** Before writing any routing code, settle where "kind of work" lives (a ticket field that records its source, like `sources.model`) and who sets it. Then make the preview answer for the *ticket*: path, model, and where each came from. Build the writing path on its own kinds, outside the code selector's rules. Pin `implementation`'s resolution as unchanged with the witness-test pattern.

**On the symptom:** the plainer brief also helped. Model choice is only part of what happened on 7 Nov, so routing alone may not reproduce it.

## Survey global: LIN-4348 @ e63c2f69d

**Where it lands.** In the routing area: the job list (`lib/llm-jobs.js`, 22 agent jobs in six groups), the routing table (`lib/model-routing*.js`: a job's own row, then its group's), `resolveRoutingWithSources` in `lib/dispatch-factory.js`, and Home's run control with its decision panel. This area is getting better. Between LIN-3852 and LIN-4177, three places that each chose a model became one table, one panel and one cost read. The stage side (`prompt-template-defs.js`, `stage-router.js`) keeps growing, and prompt size is frozen.

**The deeper point.** Routing is keyed on the *stage*, and every stage is shaped for code. An essay goes through `implementation` and gets whatever that job's row or the `make` group's row says. The Haiku is a row in each workspace's table, not a default in code, so "does the code default still fit" is a question about that row. Fresh readers exist only as subagents inside a writer's session. They have no stage, their cost is billed to the writer, and Home never shows them.

**Done the obvious way.** A "work type" check that overrides the model would add a second resolution tier and a second classifier. That brings back two places choosing a model, which LIN-3820 just removed.

The way that fits is two new stages, `write` and `fresh-read`. Each describes itself, so the selector can choose it. The table, panel, preview and spend then follow with no extra work. Going by LIN-4248, tests catch the job-list census, the template count in `source-map.md`, the prompt-size budget, the task-page golden file and the e2e templates spec. Nothing catches `stage-writes`, `proxy-preamble`, `completion-signals`, `run-view`, `wall-clock-summary`, `stage-intent`, `llms.txt` or `proxy-instructions`.

**Traps.**
1. A job with no row of its own follows its group. If `write` sits in `make`, it gets Haiku, and the "Opus without setting it by hand" goal fails with no error. Seed its own row as a logged change with a reason (as `SEEDED_ENTRY` does).
2. Judging work is split across groups. `review` and `plan-review` are in `judge`, but `look-into` and the Surveys (likely the "look-first" step) are in `plan`. Moving them is a data edit that no test catches, and it quietly changes the model they resolve to. Log the move.

**Path before running.** Home already shows one step's stage and model, with where each comes from, and has Change. What's new is showing the whole *path* (write → read). Work it out from the stage routes rather than keeping a second hand-written list.

**Better, and this task can afford it:** the two stages, rows seeded with reasons, and the fresh reader as a stage that can be seen, priced and routed.

**Better still, but not this task's:** stage names and selector rules assume code throughout, and writing is only the first kind of work that doesn't fit. `docs/plans/llm-routing-design.md` also records an SD issue: a cold resume sends no `--model`. A writer resumed cold would run on Claude Code's default, not Opus.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

Err larger, John's standing answer.

The Surveys agree that routing knows the step, not the kind of work, and that every step is shaped for code. They also agree that a separate override picking a model by kind of work would bring back two places choosing a model, which LIN-3820 has only just taken away. So the kind of work belongs to the ticket, along with where that came from: a person, or a guess that's visible and cheap to change. Writing gets its own steps, a writer and then a fresh reader, which route, price and show like any other step. They run on Opus at a minimum, and nothing falls back to the building default without anyone noticing. Code that an essay touches, such as figures and scripts, still gets reviewed. Before a run, the ticket shows its whole path and the model for each step, worked out from the routes rather than kept as a second list.

The Surveys found two traps that would quietly defeat this, and this ticket takes both on. A writer resumed cold is sent no model; see `docs/plans/llm-routing-design.md`. That fix is in **simple-dispatcher**, so this ticket now covers both repositories, and simple-dispatcher's rule applies: runtime behaviour needs a runtime witness. The second trap is that the runner kit can't map "fable", though Fable counts as Opus or better.

Two things stay with John. Whether the look-first and judging steps should move to a model suited to judgement is a cost decision, so raise it as a ruling with the cost difference. Whether Haiku still fits as the code default is not this ticket's to change; say in the pull request what you think.

This runs after LIN-4345 lands, because both change the stage templates and the prompt size budget.

**Done when** an essay ticket filed in plain words runs writer, then fresh reader, on Opus with nobody setting the model, and the ticket showed that path before it ran. A code ticket's path and model are unchanged. The model was only part of what made the 7 November essay work, so done also means the essay reads well, not just that the right model ran.

**Update from John (7 Nov, ~10:15 UTC):** for now everything new runs on Opus. The loop working matters more than its cost, and tuning down comes later. The routing table now has every agent step on Opus: the job overrides for implementation, plan, close-out, autopilot and triage are cleared to their group (routing log entries 22–26). So the cost ruling in point 5 of the size call isn't needed, and the Haiku code default is moot for now. The rest of the size call stands: the kind of work on the ticket, the writer and fresh-reader steps with their path shown before a run, and the two traps.

## Parked until the round-1 discussion

Round 1 (LIN-4344) is stopping at the work already in flight, so this ticket hasn't started. It moves to the next set, alongside the real work (costs and UI). As real product work, it's a fair test of the new loop. No action needed until then.
